All 54 patients analyzed had heterozygous variants in TNFAIP3, comprising a total of 35 distinct pathogenic variants.
Pathological findings in the third patient (patient 53) showed extensive hepatocyte loss (suspicious of atrophy of the liver parenchyma).

phenotype_specificity.statement: Person-level: autoimmune features (type 1 diabetes, suspected AIH, Hashimoto's disease) and acneiform lesions, without recurrent fever or ulcers in the survey table. Exclusion of other genes is not stated.

segregation.statement: No affected relative is reported. The pedigree figure text of 40574834 shows an asymptomatic-carrier symbol (†) in the family 36 panel, but the layout is garbled; the panel should check Supplementary Figure 1.

quotes.quote: Additionally, family analysis revealed that three cases with heterozygous variants were asymptomatic (penetrance: 95.7%).

functional.statement: No assay result for this specific variant is stated in the text of 40574834. The paper says newly identified variants were tested with an NF-kB reporter assay in A20-deficient HEK293 cells (construct) and shown in Figure 2, and that diagnosis required functional confirmation, but the figure's variant labels are not in the text available here. These quotes are cohort-level.

quotes.quote: The results of functional analyses of newly identified TNFAIP3 variants are shown in Figure 2 and Supplementary Figure 2.
The diagnosis of HA20 was confirmed via functional analysis of the TNFAIP3 variant.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Frameshift (5-nt duplication), predicted p.(Cys612TrpfsTer87) per the batch HGVS. The paper attributes the disease to heterozygous loss-of-function variants.

quotes.quote: A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is a hereditary autoinflammatory disease caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in the TNFAIP3 gene (1).
All 54 patients analyzed had heterozygous variants in TNFAIP3, comprising a total of 35 distinct pathogenic variants.

concerns: Carrier possibly missing from the batch: an asymptomatic heterozygous carrier symbol (†) appears in the family 36 pedigree text (layout garbled).
Phenotype is mainly autoimmune (type 1 diabetes, AIH suspected, Hashimoto's) rather than the fever-and-ulcer pattern; the panel may weigh specificity.
Survey tables only; no case narrative.
notes_for_panel: Single proband; possible asymptomatic carrier relative per pedigree symbol. Penetrance in the cohort is stated as 95.7% (three asymptomatic heterozygous carriers), without naming families in the text.
